sections.content: The neutral word order for a description is subject then predicate adjective: 'Ez a ruha szép' (This dress is pretty). Hungarian can also put the adjective first, before the demonstrative and noun, to make an exclamation -- the meaning shifts from a plain statement to admiration.

Both sentences are correct zero-copula statements -- no van appears either way. Fronting szép just adds emphasis, the way English might say 'Pretty, this dress!' instead of the flat 'This dress is pretty.'
